review_title: Surgical methods for first trimester termination of pregnancy
screening_criteria: Randomised controlled trials comparing different surgical methods for first trimester abortion were eligible.
gold_label_policy_description: dataset labels 1.0 and 0.5 count as INCLUDE; 0.0 counts as EXCLUDE

studies.study_title: Early complication after induced first‐trimaster abortion
studies.predicted_reason: This is an observational study analyzing complications in 5,851 consecutively induced abortions. It does not compare different surgical methods and is not a randomized controlled trial.

studies.study_title: Manual vacuum aspiration, a safe and effective alternative in early pregnancy termination
studies.predicted_reason: Randomized controlled trial comparing conventional vacuum aspiration (VA) vs manual vacuum aspiration (MVA) for first trimester abortion (gestational age <56 days). 200 women randomized to either surgical method.

studies.study_title: Induced termination of pregnancy before and after Roe v Wade. Trends in the mortality and morbidity of women
studies.predicted_reason: This is a historical epidemiological analysis using national statistics data to compare mortality/morbidity trends before and after Roe v Wade. Not a randomized trial and does not compare surgical methods.

This RCT compares prostaglandin suppository vs placebo for cervical preparation BEFORE vacuum aspiration. All women received the same surgical method (vacuum aspiration). The intervention being tested is preoperative medication, not different surgical methods.

studies.study_title: A comparison of D&C and vacuum aspiration for performing first trimester abortion
studies.predicted_reason: Randomized controlled trial comparing dilatation and curettage (D&C) vs vacuum aspiration for first trimester abortion. 420 women randomly assigned to either surgical method.

studies.study_title: Acceptability of manual versus electric aspiration for first trimester abortion: a randomised trial
studies.predicted_reason: Randomized controlled trial comparing manual vacuum aspiration vs electric vacuum aspiration for first trimester abortion (<10 weeks). 84 women randomized to either surgical method.

studies.study_title: Similarities in women's perception and acceptability of manual vacuum aspiration and electric vacuum aspiration for first trimester abortion.
studies.predicted_reason: Randomized controlled trial comparing manual vacuum aspiration (MVA) vs electric vacuum aspiration (EVA) for first trimester abortion. 127 women randomly assigned to either surgical method.

studies.study_title: Abortion by means of suction curettage compared to conventional metal curette
studies.predicted_reason: While this study compares vacuum aspiration vs dilatation and curettage, the abstract does not state that randomization was used. It describes 47 women undergoing abortion with 23 by vacuum aspiration and 24 by D&C, but does not explicitly mention randomization. Without clear evidence of RCT design, this study is excluded.

studies.study_title: First trimester abortion by vacuum aspiration
studies.predicted_reason: This RCT compares metal vs flexible plastic cannulae for performing vacuum aspiration. Both groups received the same surgical method (vacuum aspiration); the comparison is between equipment types within the same technique, not between different surgical methods.

studies.study_title: Comparison of pain and time of procedure with two first trimester abortion techniques performed by residents and faculty
studies.predicted_reason: Randomized controlled trial comparing manual vacuum aspirator vs electric vacuum curettage for first trimester abortion. 114 women randomized to either surgical method.
